title: Check if Numbers Are Ascending in a Sentence
statement: Return true if all numbers appearing in the sentence are strictly increasing.
explanation: Extract numeric tokens and compare each with the previous number.
example: s="1 box has 3 blue 4 red 6 green and 12 yellow" -> true

title: Kth Distinct String in an Array
approach: Scan distinct values in original order
statement: Return the kth string that occurs exactly once, or an empty string if fewer than k exist.
explanation: Count each string, then scan the original array and decrement k only for frequency-one entries.

title: Smallest Index With Equal Value
approach: Find first index matching value modulo ten
statement: Return the smallest i for which i modulo 10 equals nums[i], or -1.
explanation: Scan indices from left to right and return the first match.

title: Count Vowel Substrings of a String
statement: Count substrings consisting only of vowels and containing all five vowels.
explanation: For each start, extend until a consonant; track distinct vowels and count every window containing all five.

title: Time Needed to Buy Tickets
statement: Return the time until person k finishes buying tickets, with one ticket sold per turn in queue order.
explanation: People before or at k can buy at most tickets[k] turns; people after k can buy one fewer turn.

title: Count Common Words With One Occurrence
statement: Count words that occur exactly once in each of two arrays.
explanation: Count frequencies in both arrays and count words whose frequency is one in both.

title: Finding 3-Digit Even Numbers
statement: Return all unique three-digit even numbers that can be formed from the given digits, sorted ascending.
explanation: Choose three distinct positions, require a nonzero hundreds digit and an even units digit, and deduplicate results.

title: Rings and Rods
statement: Count rods that contain at least one red, green, and blue ring.
explanation: Track the three possible colors for each rod and count rods with all three.

title: Maximum Number of Words Found in Sentences
statement: Return the maximum word count among the sentences.
explanation: Split each sentence into words, count them, and retain the maximum.
example: sentences=["alice and bob love leetcode","i think so too","this is great thanks very much"] -> 6

title: A Number After a Double Reversal
statement: Return true if reversing the digits twice restores the original number.
explanation: Every positive number without a trailing zero is unchanged by double reversal; zero also qualifies.
